0.content:
Lyney, Lynette's twin and the trio's leader, is Freminet's adoptive older brother. When the twins arrived at the Hotel Bouffes d'ete, Lynette broke the water pump; Lyney half-fixed it, and Freminet, the reticent maintenance boy, finished the job and apologised for not replacing the old parts. Lyney became his assistant in the Hotel's small workroom, and they became friends. As a child Freminet called him "Brother"; later he switched to "Lyney", feeling like a spare part beside the telepathic-seeming twins. He can tell Lyney wears a brave face, and once told him he need not wear a mask all the time; they argued, and he never raised it again. Lyney shows him magic tricks at home just to make him smile.

In 4.6 Lyney caught him lying about extra food, learned he was hiding Clervie, and in private told him: they had stood by each other for years, and to him that meant more than blood; Freminet and Lynette were the most important people in his life. Freminet cried; Paimon noticed. They sealed a promise with their childhood fist bump, and Lynette joined in. For the Hotel's Founding Day show Lyney entrusted him with every magic prop, and when Lyney rescued a Maison Gardiennage official who worked for the Hotel, using a smoke-and-glider diversion, it was Freminet who fished the man out of the Fleuve Cendre.

1.content:
Lynette, Lyney's twin, is Freminet's adoptive older sister. She notices when he looks downcast and turns up with tea or a bandage; she tells him everyone has strengths and the whole House relies on him to fix things. She ruins nearly every machine she touches, and he is usually the one who arrives to repair it. Because she dislikes busywork, he had an automated feeder custom-made for the House's growing number of small animals. She calls him delicate and gentle but prone to belittling himself, and she bridges his clashes with Lyney.

After a successful mission with the twins she filled his cup and offered him her dessert: "We're family." She sets him riddles while blowing on her tea. In 4.6 she ambushed the brothers' secret pact and joined it. In 7.1 at Podvorye Restaurant he noticed she had fallen asleep while eating. Petting a Blubberbeast, he decided, was a world removed from petting Lynette's cat.

2.content:
Freminet calls Arlecchino "Father". She replaced the cruel previous director, and under her failure no longer meant punishment. She recovered his mother's pendant from the moneylenders' base, saw the lie he had been told and gave him the truth, then left the room so he could grieve. She teaches that every child matters and must value their own life, which he finds harder than obedience. She dislikes tears, so he cries only underwater. She sees a complex mind in him that hides its emotions and blames itself for things that are not its doing.

In 4.6 he defied her by hiding Clervie, then fought her beside the twins and the Traveler ("I'm sorry, 'Father'-"); they lost and he was bedridden for two days, but he refused her memory-erasing potion. Afterward he told the Traveler he had thanked her for everything and that, had she not taken over the House, he probably would not have survived; he vowed the trio would follow her "whether the path before us is bathed in sunlight or shrouded in shadow." She sent the trio into Meropide (4.1), to Nod-Krai (6.1) and on Snezhnaya missions (7.1).

3.comment: Freminet: Freminet's mother and the music-box pendant
3.content:
His mother worked from dawn to dusk to pay his absent father's debts. When the boy fixed a dead wall clock, she praised him; next morning it was gone, and that evening she brought bread he still remembers. After that she brought him broken clockwork to "wake", and it always vanished the next day. One day she found a thumb-sized music-box pendant by the road that still played; every night she took it from her neck and they listened together. When the moneylenders demanded the house and the boy, she took him to the House of the Hearth, the one place they could not reach him, said "Be a good boy", and faced them alone. Years later "Father" returned the pendant, rusted, silent and stained with dried blood.

He keeps it. He read that the dead become stars and watch over the living, and wonders whether she would be disappointed that the child she protected with her life is still so timid. He hates his father for abandoning them.

4.content:
Pers is the small clockwork penguin Freminet built and named after the hero of a picture book: a black-and-white bird who stuttered, wobbled and could not fly, was bullied, sank with a wrecked ship, discovered he could "fly" by swimming, and restored a stolen diadem to the undersea palace to calm a storm. Freminet admired that Pers but was struck most by his loneliness, so he decided to "stick close and hug Pers" so they could keep each other warm. He says Pers is more like family than a toy, that they grew up together, and he keeps adding functions in the hope that Pers will one day fly. Pers keeps him company on lonely nights and fights beside him.

During thunderstorms he reassures Pers: "Don't be scared, Pers. I'll keep you safe." Pers, his Vision and his helmet are where he draws strength. In 6.7 he asked Sandrone to review his improvement ideas, and offered Pers to Citlali as something to hug.

5.comment: Freminet: Crucabena and the old House of the Hearth
5.content: Crucabena ("Mother"), the previous director, ran the House as a place where orphans fought and the injured were discarded. She brought Freminet in, later told him he had been sold to settle a debt and abandoned, and threatened his mother's safety if he disobeyed. He learned that members must be ready to give their lives for the family, followed orders unthinkingly to escape punishment, and was sent behind enemy lines because no one suspected him. His habit of retreating into the sea began then. He arrived after her experiments had ended and she never spoke of the past to newcomers. Arlecchino killed her and burned her files.

6.content: On a routine underwater mission with other House children, Freminet sensed something wrong and signalled everyone to surface. Their diving equipment was failing. Drowsy and slipping away, he thought there was no point surviving to a hopeless life among "family" who felt like clockwork meka. Then a slow, stuttering voice called his name, like Pers from the stories. He resolved to abandon no one, felt strength return, and brought all of them up. Only afterward did he find a crystal-clear Cryo Vision on his divesuit. He has never told anyone what really happened, because true heroes are not in it for recognition.

7.comment: Freminet: The Fortress of Meropide and the prophecy trial
7.content: In 4.0 Freminet helped Lyney's show preparations, was too shy to deliver supplies to Estelle at Beaumont Workshop, and told Paimon the legend that rain falls when Fontaine's Hydro Dragon weeps. In 4.1 the trio entered the Fortress of Meropide to find Childe for "Father". As the best diver, Freminet swam the flooded tunnel Childe had taken, was overcome by Primordial Seawater, turned back and collapsed. Wriothesley had locked the route so Lyney could not follow into danger; Clorinde carried Freminet out and Sigewinne treated him. On waking he warned the group of what he had found. In 4.2 he joined the plan to expose Furina and, after the verdict, appeared with the missing first prophecy slate. Afterward he was at Romaritime Harbor with the twins when Arlecchino held the Hydro Gnosis.

8.comment: Freminet: Clervie and the duel with "Father"
8.content: When rumours of a "phantom child" moved the House's Fontaine members to Poisson, Freminet was caught asking for extra food, water and clean cloth. He had hidden a ghostly girl, Clervie, behind the Spina di Rosula headquarters for half a month, believing she was the voice that had woken him the year before to save the poisoned Chapleau: "She's been living with us, helping us from the shadows... I think that makes her family." He had tried taking her far away, but she always reappeared wherever the House went. Lyney and Lynette joined him; he asked around among House members. At Mont Esus East, when Arlecchino moved to execute the "traitors", he sided with Lyney and fought her with the twins and the Traveler. They lost; the departing members drank a potion erasing their House memories, while the trio declined theirs.

9.content: In 6.1, after an attack on Sandrone's Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau in Nod-Krai, "Father" sent the trio to help. Freminet's quiet "Do you need a hand?" made Sandrone recognise him; she called him over to help her fix her machines while banishing Lynette from them, and when Lyney left the work to him he answered, "You've got it." In 6.7, at a tea party outside the Hotel Bouffes d'ete, he said "Father" had told them not to disturb her, then nervously asked her to look at his ideas for Pers. She agreed, and he thanked "Lady Sandrone". He wondered aloud whether getting along with others is a must-have skill for a Harbinger. Sandrone said she envied their little family.

10.content: In Chapter VII Act III (One Move Left to Make), the Traveler and Paimon met the trio at Podvorye Restaurant. Freminet greeted them with "It's been a while..." Lyney explained they had been on a House mission with "Father", gathering intel and preparing "surprises" for officials looking to defect, and had a few days off while she met The Jester at the Armory Palace. Lyney sent Freminet to keep Lynette from ordering too many desserts. They were visibly exhausted. After borscht Freminet murmured "...Warm..." and noticed Lynette had fallen asleep mid-meal. In 7.0 he is only mentioned, by Paimon, as someone good with machines.

11.comment: Freminet: Diving, the sea and the secret base
11.content: Diving is how Freminet escapes. He spends more time with the Tidalga than with people, because they float quietly and never act disappointed; he pours out his feelings to the Romaritime Flowers, the only ones who hear him cry. He loses track of time studying the fossil patterns of Beryl Conches and wonders whether Lumitoile are drawn to people the way Cicins are to light. Near a spot of extraordinary beauty he built a secret underwater base and keeps glowing sea creatures there as pets. He likes the sea because, from deep enough, even the sun is soft on the eyes.
